Rashi on Pesachim 107a:10:1.english: A cup of blessing - Grace after Meals.

Rashi on Pesachim 107a:11:1.hebrew: מטעמת יין בכל הוא - אותה טעימה שאמרו, המברך צריך שיטעום בכל שהוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 107a:11:1.english: Tasting any amount of wine - [Regarding] that tasting that they mentioned, the one who recites the blessing must taste any amount.

Rashi on Pesachim 107a:13:1.hebrew: מנחה גדולה - (משבע) שעות ומחצה ולמעלה, זמן הקרבת תמיד כשאתה בא להקדימו:
Rashi on Pesachim 107a:13:1.english: Greater minḥa - (From seven) and a half hours and upward — [which is] the time of offering the daily burnt offering [tamid] when you come to advance it.

Rashi on Pesachim 107a:14:1.english: And because of the Paschal [offering] - Lest he sit at the meal and refrain and neglect to make the Paschal [offering].

Rashi on Pesachim 107a:1:1.hebrew: כל השבת - כדאמרן לעיל, עד יום רביעי:
Rashi on Pesachim 107a:1:1.english: The entire week - As we said above, until Wednesday.

Rashi on Pesachim 107a:5:1.hebrew: פירזומא - שכר שעורים, בלשון לעז ברוי"ש (בריי"ש: שְׁכַר שְׂעוֹרִים (מין בירה)):
Rashi on Pesachim 107a:5:1.english: Pirzuma - Barley beer; in Old French, brois (breis: barley beer (a type of beer)).

Rashi on Pesachim 107a:7:1.hebrew: בר תליסר מגני - שנתנו מים על התמרים, ואחר שזבו נתן על תמרים אחרים, וכן הביא תמרים עד י"ג פעמים:
Rashi on Pesachim 107a:7:1.english: Of thirteen soakings - That they put water on the dates, and after it drained, he put [it] on other dates, and so he brought dates up to thirteen times.

Rashi on Pesachim 107a:7:2.hebrew: מייסרן ומפייס - מצערין, ובשעת שתיה מפייסין הן; כלומר, טובים הן, וראוי לומר עליהן קידוש והבדלה:
Rashi on Pesachim 107a:7:2.english: It pains and soothes - [They] cause pain, and at the time of drinking they are soothing; that is to say, they are good, and it is fit to recite Kiddush and Havdalah over them.

Rashi on Pesachim 107a:8:1.english: I will take a vow in public - A vow that has no nullification.

Rashi on Pesachim 107a:9:1.hebrew: שרי ליה אבא - התחלת לעשות שכר ולהשתכר בו מערב, לכך הוא יפה בעיניך ומקדש אתה עליו:
Rashi on Pesachim 107a:9:1.english: Abba has begun - You have begun to make beer and to profit from it from the evening; therefore it is pleasing in your eyes, and you recite kiddush over it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:11:1.hebrew: אם טעם מלא לוגמא יצא - וכדמפרש ביומא (דף פ.): "כל שאילו מסלקו לצד אחד יראה כמלא לוגמיו", והוי פחות מרביעית כדאמרינן התם. אבל "מלא לוגמיו" — אמרינן התם דהוי יותר מרביעית. ונראה שהוא רוב רביעית, דאמרינן לקמן: "והוא דשתה רובא דכסא". ודוקא לאדם בינוני, אבל לעוג מלך הבשן בעי טפי, כדאמרינן התם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:11:1.english: If he tasted a cheekful, he has fulfilled [his obligation] - And as [the Gemara] explains in Yoma (80a): "Any [amount] such that if one shifts it to one side [of his mouth], it appears like a cheekful," and it is less than a revi'it, as we say there. However, [regarding] "his cheekful" (melo lugmav) — we say there that it is more than a revi'it. And it appears that it [the required amount] is the majority of a revi'it, as we say later: "Provided that he drank the majority of the cup." And [this applies] specifically to an average person, but for Og, King of Bashan, more is required, as we say there.

Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:13:1.hebrew: סמוך למנחה - תימה, אמאי קרי ליה מנחה? דאי משום דמנחה היתה קריבה בין הערבים, הלא גם בשחר קריבה מנחת חביתין ומנחת תמיד? וי"ל: בשחר יש שם אחר — תפלת שחרית. ועוד, דאמרינן בפרק קמא דברכות (דף ו:): "הוי זהיר בתפלת מנחה, שאף אליהו לא נענה אלא בתפלת מנחה". ושמא בשעת הקרבת מנחה נענה, ולכך קרי ליה "תפלת מנחה", שאז היה שעת רצון:
Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:13:1.english: Adjacent to Minchah - This is puzzling: why is it called minchah? For if [it is] because a meal-offering [minchah] was offered in the afternoon, were not the griddle-cake meal-offering [chavitin] and the meal-offering of the daily offering [tamid] also offered in the morning? And one can answer: In the morning it has another name — the Shacharit [morning] prayer. Furthermore, as we say in the first chapter of Berakhot (6b): "Be careful with the Minchah prayer, for even Elijah was answered only at the Minchah prayer." And perhaps he was answered at the time of the offering of the meal-offering, and therefore it was called "the Minchah prayer," because that was a time of [divine] favor.

Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:1:1.english: Rava said: The halakha is that one who tasted [food] may recite kiddush - And so is the halakha.

Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:2:1.hebrew: אמימר מתני לה כו' - בסוף מילתיה גרסינן: "מבדיל והולך כל היום כולו", דאי לאו הכי היינו לישנא קמא. והלכה כלישנא קמא, דמבדיל עד רביעי בשבת כדאמר רבי חייא לעיל; ובתשעה באב שחל להיות במוצ"ש נמי רגילין להבדיל אחר התענית, וכן בסדר דרב עמרם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:2:1.english: Ameimar taught it, etc. - At the end of his statement, we read [the text as]: "he recites havdala throughout the entire day," for if not so, it would be [identical to] the first formulation. And the halakha is in accordance with the first formulation, that one may recite havdala until Wednesday, as Rabbi Ḥiyya said above; and on Tisha B'Av that falls on the conclusion of Shabbat as well, it is customary to recite havdala after the fast, and so [it is written] in Seder Rav Amram.

Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:4:1.hebrew: ושמע מינה מבדיל כל השבת כולה - לא שמעינן מינה אלא כל היום, אלא נקט הכי משום דהלכה כן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:4:1.english: And learn from it [that one] recites havdala the entire week - We only learn from it [that one may do so] the entire day; rather, [the Gemara] phrased it this way because the halakha is so.

Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:8:1.hebrew: אדור ברבים כו' - דקסבר דברבים אין לו הפרה, ואין הלכה כן, אלא דוקא על דעת רבים אין לו הפרה; ובמקום אחר מפורש (גיטין דף לו.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 107a:8:1.english: "I will take a vow in public," etc. - For [Rav Yosef] holds that [a vow made] in public has no annulment. However, the halakhah is not so; rather, specifically [a vow made] with the consent of the public has no annulment, and [this] is explained elsewhere (Gittin 36a).
